title: Uneven spacing between desktops when fractionally scaled
line: With fractional scaling, the gaps between the desktops in the Pager are now all the same width.
explanation: The Pager's desktops have whole logical pixel sizes and a 1 logical pixel gap. At 125% or 150% each desktop-plus-gap step is a fractional number of device pixels (e.g. 61.25), so every cell starts at a different sub-pixel offset and the rendered gaps come out 1 or 2 pixels wide depending on the panel height. The Grid now sets columnSpacing/rowSpacing so each cell plus its gap is a whole number of device pixels (using the window's effective devicePixelRatio), which makes every gap render identically; cell sizes are unchanged.

commits.message:
applets/pager: keep desktop spacing even with fractional scaling

Desktops were laid out with a one logical pixel gap, so at scales like
125% each step ended on a fraction of a device pixel and gaps were drawn
1 or 2 pixels wide. Round each step to a whole device pixel instead.

BUG: 483623

patches.diff:
From 733438e9e269567cc3fa93f30e22fda91f5ee74f Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: =?UTF-8?q?Niccol=C3=B2=20Venerandi?= <niccolo@venerandi.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 12:45:33 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] applets/pager: keep desktop spacing even with fractional
 scaling

Desktops were laid out with a one logical pixel gap, so at scales like
125% each step ended on a fraction of a device pixel and gaps were drawn
1 or 2 pixels wide. Round each step to a whole device pixel instead.

BUG: 483623
---
 applets/pager/qml/main.qml | 9 +++++++++
 1 file changed, 9 insertions(+)

diff --git a/applets/pager/qml/main.qml b/applets/pager/qml/main.qml
index b4211ddbbd..8010f3d504 100644
--- a/applets/pager/qml/main.qml
+++ b/applets/pager/qml/main.qml
@@ -243,6 +243,8 @@ PlasmoidItem {
 
         anchors.centerIn: parent
         spacing: 1
+        columnSpacing: spacingToWholeDevicePixels(columnWidth)
+        rowSpacing: spacingToWholeDevicePixels(rowHeight)
         rows: effectiveRows * effectiveColumns >= pagerModel.count ? effectiveRows : pagerModel.count
         columns: effectiveRows * effectiveColumns >= pagerModel.count ? effectiveColumns : pagerModel.count
 
@@ -302,6 +304,13 @@ PlasmoidItem {
             }
         ]
 
+        readonly property real devicePixelRatio: Window.window?.devicePixelRatio ?? 1
+
+        // With fractional scaling, end each cell plus its gap on a device pixel, so that all gaps look the same
+        function spacingToWholeDevicePixels(cellSize: int): real {
+            return Math.round((cellSize + spacing) * devicePixelRatio) / devicePixelRatio - cellSize;
+        }
+
         property int innerSpacing: (effectiveRows - 1) * spacing
         property int rowHeight: Math.floor((root.height - innerSpacing) / effectiveRows)
         property int columnWidth: Math.floor(rowHeight * pagerItemSizeRatio)
--

reviews.text: Using Window.window?.devicePixelRatio to align each Pager cell-plus-gap step to whole device pixels is a clever and lightweight approach that works well at 125% and 150%. However, using plain Math.round((cellSize + spacing) * devicePixelRatio) can round the step below cellSize * devicePixelRatio + 1 at fractional scales between 105% and 120% (e.g. 110%, 115%, 120%, which are standard 5% increments in Plasma), leaving under 1 device pixel of gap so all desktop separators can collapse to 0 device pixels depending on the grid's subpixel origin.
changes: In applets/pager/qml/main.qml spacingToWholeDevicePixels(), ensure the rounded device-pixel step leaves at least 1 device pixel of gap (e.g. Math.max(Math.round((cellSize + spacing) * devicePixelRatio), Math.ceil(cellSize * devicePixelRatio + 1)) / devicePixelRatio - cellSize) so scales between 105% and 120% cannot collapse gaps to 0 device pixels.
Extend the verification sweep to include at least one scale in the 105%–120% range (e.g. 110% or 120%) in addition to 125% and 150%.
